synthesis:
Production incident: scout:record-check-ins (DEV-2313, scheduled every 5 min) exhausted production host memory (~29GB marginal against ~30GB headroom) and forced a full host reboot on 2026-08-12. Root-cause chain: (1) sc_positions is read via lower(kit_mapping), which cannot use the table's case-sensitive (kit_mapping, timestamp_utc) ORDER BY, so every position-window read scans ~3056/32732 granules instead of ~13/32732 (chlocal-owned, W1, out of scope here); (2) one org has ~255k open order addresses, chunked at 2000/kit; (3) the ACTUAL amplifier is that the recorder pulls that whole per-org address list into a PHP array and re-serializes it as a ClickHouse values() SQL literal for every kit -> ~5,500 CH queries per cycle; (4) cycles run 36-209 min against a 5-min schedule whose withoutOverlapping(10) is a lock EXPIRY, not a duration cap, so a new process spawns roughly every 10 minutes once cycles outlive it, driving concurrency to ~17 simultaneous processes; (5) each process holds its own O(addresses_per_org) PHP array (re-copied whole by array_chunk() per kit, plus an unbounded $matches[] accumulator), so total host memory is O(addresses x concurrent processes) with concurrency itself unbounded -- that product took the host down. The schedule has been disabled in production since commit 11bc23e2 and stays disabled until concrete criteria are met.

The intended outcome of this PR (W2+W3 of the plan of record) is to rewrite the matcher so the entire match -- address enumeration, GPS proximity join, and dedup -- happens in ONE ClickHouse statement per org/kit, lifting ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's already-proven CTE architecture (adapted from clarity.scans_hot/cold + org_id/kit_id to clarity.sc_positions + lower(kit_mapping)), so PHP only ever receives the handful of actual matches (~40/cycle) instead of the full address list, plus a hard concurrency ceiling that holds independent of runtime (replacing the ineffective withoutOverlapping(10) TTL). The chlocal-owned sc_positions projection (W1) and the operational schedule re-enable + host-memory verification (W4) are explicitly out of scope for this repo/PR.

scope.summary: Rewrite ScoutCheckInMatchQuery to do address enumeration (hotlist FINAL -> public_hotlist_address -> public_address) and the sc_positions proximity match in one ClickHouse CTE chain per the ScoutCheckInRollupQuery pattern, eliminating the PHP-side address array and the values()-injection round trip entirely (AC1). Add a hard, runtime-independent concurrency ceiling to the command (AC4). Fix the silent-failure problem so a failed ClickHouse read is distinguishable from a legitimately empty one (AC7) -- by having the recorder call the query classes' handle() directly instead of query(), since query()'s catch(\Throwable) swallows to [] in production/testing and a prior attempt at this exact problem (an 'advance-on-clean-pass' watermark guard, see notes) was proven dead code for exactly that reason. Add a peak-memory regression test at prod-representative scale (AC6) and a parity test against ScoutCheckInRollupQuery (AC9). W1 (the chlocal sc_positions projection) and W4 (re-enabling the schedule in production + host verification) are out of scope for this repo.

proposed_changes.change: Rewrite handle()/matchChunk() to remove the addresses-array parameter and the values()-injection CTE, replacing it with a self-contained CTE chain lifted from ScoutCheckInRollupQuery: open_hotlists (clarity.hotlist FINAL, org/staging filter) -> address_links (zod.public_hotlist_address) -> pruned addresses (zod.public_address, id IN (subquery) + extract()/toFloat64OrNull, NOT readWKTPoint) -> bbox-prefiltered against position_window (clarity.sc_positions, lower(kit_mapping)) -> geoDistance join -> GROUP BY (address_id, hour_bucket). Keep the existing outer SELECT's direct-preference argMin(hotlist_id, (toUInt8(is_staged), hotlist_id)) / min(is_staged) logic verbatim -- it is already correct and does not need to change. Prefer self::zodDb() dynamically (like ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery) rather than hardcoding 'zod.' the way ScoutCheckInRollupQuery does.
proposed_changes.reason: AC1 -- this is the ticket's designated 'architecture to lift' (the docblock's own DEV-1758 lift point) and the direct fix for the PHP round-trip amplifier.

proposed_changes.change: Becomes unused by the recorder once enumeration moves inside the combined match query -- no other caller exists anywhere in the repo. Recommend removing it (with its docblock's {@see} references updated) or clearly marking it orphaned; do not leave dead code silently.
proposed_changes.reason: AC1 explicitly forbids any per-org address list crossing PHP, which is this class's entire purpose for the recorder.

proposed_changes.change: Remove openOrderAddressesForOrg() and the per-org address cache. Call the rewritten ScoutCheckInMatchQuery::handle() DIRECTLY (bypassing ::query()'s try/catch swallow) so a genuine ClickHouse failure propagates into the existing per-org/per-kit catch blocks instead of silently becoming []. Replace the per-match firstOrCreate() loop with a single ScoutCheckIn::insertOrIgnore($rows) bulk write per kit/org against the existing unique(kit_id,address_id,hour_bucket) index (insertOrIgnore returns the inserted-row count, so the existing $recorded accounting still works, but created_at/updated_at must now be stamped manually since insertOrIgnore bypasses model events). Add the W3 concurrency ceiling at the top of handle().

acceptance_criteria.item: AC1: Match computed server-side in CH; no per-org address list crosses PHP; no re-serialization to SQL.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Core of W2; directly fixes the measured amplifier (~5,500 CH queries/cycle -> the values() round trip).

acceptance_criteria.item: AC2: Duration — full cycle at prod cardinality < 5-min cadence, measured.
acceptance_criteria.reason: The code change targets this, but 'measured' at true production cardinality cannot be fully closed from this repo/PR — it needs either a chlocal-side EXPLAIN/query_log comparison or a staged prod-like run, and Design Risk 2 (bbox selectivity vs GPS density, unmeasured) means the code change alone does not guarantee the number. Implement the code; treat the measurement as a follow-up gate before AC8's re-enable.

acceptance_criteria.item: AC3: Memory — peak RSS O(matches), budget stated; peak x plausible concurrency fits ~30GB headroom.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Achieved architecturally by removing the PHP address array (O(addresses) -> O(matches)); needs a stated budget number backed by AC6's test.

acceptance_criteria.item: AC4: Concurrency — hard ceiling independent of runtime; lookback invariant holds.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Required by the incident's own root-cause chain (concurrency is what turned a memory-per-process cost into a host-level OOM); mechanism (semaphore vs queued jobs) left open, see questions.

acceptance_criteria.item: AC5: Projection proven — single-kit 15-min EXPLAIN granules in tens; matcher query_log p50 << 400ms, read_rows << ~500k.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Explicitly depends on the chlocal-owned W1 ALTER TABLE ... ADD PROJECTION, a separate repo/ticket; platform is SELECT-only here per evidence-38238.

acceptance_criteria.item: AC6: Regression tests — a peak-memory assertion at prod-representative address cardinality (not the current 3-address fixtures).
acceptance_criteria.reason: Zero such assertions exist in the suite today (confirmed by grep); this is the direct test-gap the incident report calls out.

acceptance_criteria.item: AC7: Silent-failure guard — ClickhouseQuery::query() swallows \Throwable to [] in prod, so a failed match looks identical to an empty one; the recorder must distinguish 'ran, empty' from 'failed'.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Recommended approach: call the query classes' handle() directly (bypassing query()'s swallow) so the recorder's own existing try/catch sees the real exception. A prior attempt that stayed behind query() (a watermark 'advance-on-clean-pass' guard) was proven dead code in this exact repo's history for this exact reason — see notes.

acceptance_criteria.item: AC8: Host verified — pct_usable flat across a full cycle after re-enable.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Explicitly operational/prod-only per the brief; cannot be satisfied from a code PR.

acceptance_criteria.item: AC9: Parity — rewritten matcher and ScoutCheckInRollupQuery agree on the same inputs (one domain rule).
acceptance_criteria.reason: No existing dedicated test for ScoutCheckInRollupQuery to extend (confirmed by search) — must be built fresh, seeding both scans_hot and sc_positions fixtures at the same location/time.

questions.q: IN (per-org batch, ~12 queries/cycle) vs equality (per-kit, ~43 queries/cycle) on lower(kit_mapping) for the rewritten matcher's position_window scope — which shape does W2 use?

Does the lifted bbox prefilter (tuned against LPR scans in ScoutCheckInRollupQuery) stay selective enough against sc_positions' much denser ~3s GPS fix rate, or does it need re-tuning for the recorder specifically?

What mechanism implements the W3 hard concurrency ceiling — an N-slot semaphore (e.g. Cache::lock) acquired at command start, or per-org queued jobs (reviving DEV-2347's dispatcher now that W2 shrinks per-org cost)? Neither has any existing precedent in this codebase (confirmed: zero Cache::lock() usage in app/Console/Commands or app/Jobs, zero WithoutOverlapping job-middleware usage anywhere).
Should ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery be deleted now that no caller remains, or kept unused for a future consumer?

Should the schedule be re-enabled (uncommented) as part of this PR once W2/W3 land, or does it need to wait for W1 (the chlocal projection) given Design Risk 2's note that BOTH the IN and equality shapes are slow on the current, unprojected sc_positions table? This directly determines how to resolve the currently-red ScoutRecordCheckInsScheduleTest.

Is bypassing ClickhouseQuery::query() (calling ::handle() directly from the recorder) the accepted AC7 fix, or should ClickhouseQuery itself gain an opt-in rethrow mode for callers that need to react to failure?
questions.source: needs-human — but see notes: a prior exception-based guard that stayed behind ::query() was proven dead code (git 2cd844090), so any design that keeps routing through ::query() should be treated with suspicion.

questions.q: Does insertOrIgnore()'s return value (count of rows actually inserted) suffice to keep the existing 'recorded' counter semantics, given the switch away from per-row firstOrCreate()/wasRecentlyCreated?
questions.answer: Yes — Laravel's Eloquent/query-builder insertOrIgnore() returns an int count of rows successfully inserted, which is a direct drop-in replacement for the current wasRecentlyCreated-based increment.

This predates this PR but must be resolved by it — either by rewriting the test to assert the intentional disabled state, or by re-enabling the schedule as part of this PR (see the corresponding question). Left as-is it will show as a failing test in this PR's CI regardless of what this ticket touches.

AC5 (projection proven) and AC8 (host verified) are structurally unsatisfiable from within this repo/PR alone — AC5 depends on a separate chlocal ticket shipping and being EXPLAIN-verified against Cloud; AC8 depends on production host observation after a real re-enable. Neither blocks writing the W2/W3 code, but neither can be closed by this ticket in isolation.

Design Risk 2 raises a real possibility that W2 alone (before W1 lands) cannot bring cycle duration under the 5-minute cadence at production cardinality, since the sc_positions PK bypass (the single largest measured cost) is orthogonal to query shape. If true, AC2/AC8 cannot be met and the schedule cannot be safely re-enabled until W1 ships in chlocal, regardless of how well W2/W3 are implemented here — this is a sequencing/scope question for a human, not a code blocker.
notes: okf/concepts/scout-check-in-recorder.md's Performance section currently states, unqualified, 'The concurrency is load-bearing.' This is the exact conclusion CLAUDE.md's WRITE-gate warning calls out as reverted/withdrawn and 'reasoning that contributed to an outage' — the incident report (evidence-38240-incident.md) is unambiguous that unbounded concurrency IS the OOM mechanism. Do not cite that wiki sentence as support for any W3 design choice; per the WRITE rule, do not edit the wiki now, but the ticket/PR should flag it for correction once the fix lands.

routes/console.php's own comment inside the (currently commented-out) schedule block repeats a milder version of the same claim ('the concurrency is currently what keeps the recorder up ... Bounding cycle duration has to come first') — also stale once W2 lands, since the throughput/latency trade-off it describes assumed the old O(addresses x chunks) per-cycle cost.

Two earlier DEV-2342 attempts (git 2cd844090, aedc2f525) already built and reverted a per-org watermark/'advance-on-clean-pass' guard aimed at exactly AC7's problem — a driver-added failing test proved it was dead code because ClickhouseQuery::query()'s swallow makes the failure flag unreachably false in production. Any AC7 design that still routes through ::query() will very likely reproduce this exact failure mode; treat AC7 as higher-risk than its one-line description suggests.

No dedicated unit test for ScoutCheckInRollupQuery exists in this repo today (confirmed by search) — the existing command test's comment 'Mirrors ScoutCheckInRollupQueryTest' (ScoutRecordCheckInsCommandTest.php:86) references a file that does not exist. Coverage of that query lives entirely in tests/Feature/Http/Controllers/Api/ClarityScoutDashboardControllerTest.php's HTTP-level tests. The AC9 parity test has no existing fixture pair to extend and must be built fresh.

ScoutCheckInRollupQuery.php hardcodes the 'zod.' database prefix literally (zod.public_hotlist_address, zod.public_address) instead of using self::zodDb() as ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery does — a known ~15-class local-CH-QA limitation. When lifting the CTE into the rewritten ScoutCheckInMatchQuery, prefer the dynamic self::zodDb() pattern (matching the class this rewrite absorbs) rather than reproducing the hardcode in new code.
Zero memory_get_peak_usage()/memory_limit assertions exist anywhere in the test suite today (confirmed by repo-wide grep) — AC6 introduces a wholly new test pattern for this codebase.

No existing command or job anywhere in this repo uses Cache::lock() or the WithoutOverlapping job middleware (confirmed by grep) — W3 has no in-repo sibling pattern to copy; whichever mechanism is chosen will be a first.

config/horizon.php's HORIZON_SUPERVISOR_1_PROCESSES / _2_PROCESSES both default to maxProcesses=1. If W3 goes the queued-job route, it will serialize by default unless a dedicated supervisor/queue with an explicit higher maxProcesses is configured — this default is exactly why DEV-2347's original job-dispatch design was reverted in commit 102a3430, though that revert predates W2 shrinking per-org cost, so the trade-off may look different now.

Kit::query()->find($driver->kit_id) inside the per-driver loop is an N+1 (one Postgres query per driver, ~43/cycle) — trivial next to the ClickHouse cost and not memory-relevant; out of scope for this ticket but a one-line eager-load opportunity if this loop is being touched anyway.

This ticket's own history is a caution against scope creep: three restarts, a 7-node DAG parked by a sizing gate (11 files/3 concerns vs threshold 6), and a 62-finding review-round failure (min score 64/100) all preceded the 'STRIP TO OBSERVABILITY ONLY' descope that shipped as PR #323. Keep this pass to W2+W3+AC6/AC7/AC9 and resist rebuilding the planner/watermark/cap machinery that was already tried and explicitly descoped twice.

Per Laravel Boost guidelines (okf/concepts/laravel-boost-guidelines.md, read in full): new/changed methods need explicit return types and constructor property promotion where applicable; run vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent before finalizing; comments should stay sparse per repo convention (user preference, also matches CLAUDE.md's 'keep comments minimal' memory note) even though the existing Scout query classes carry unusually dense docblocks — match the existing Scout-class density (it is load-bearing domain rationale, not decoration) rather than the generic minimal-comment default.

resource_envelope.growth: kits_processed went 29-32 -> 43 and orgs_processed 11 -> 12 within a single 4-hour production window (DEV-2342 evidence); any duration/memory budget must assume continued growth, not the current snapshot.
resource_envelope.allocation_sketch: Current (pre-fix): O(addresses_per_org) PHP array held per process across the 43-kit loop, re-copied whole by array_chunk() per kit (~128 chunks for the largest org), plus an unbounded $matches[] accumulator — measured 1.5-3 GB/process x up to 17 concurrent processes = ~29 GB marginal, which emptied a ~30 GB headroom and forced the host reboot. Post-W2 (this PR): PHP never materializes an address array at all — each ClickHouse call returns only the ~40 matches/cycle the ticket cites, so per-process memory should be O(matches), a small constant independent of org size. W3's job is to put a hard, runtime-independent ceiling on how many of those (now-cheap) processes can run at once, since W2 does not by itself bound concurrency — a fast-but-unbounded recorder is still exploitable if ClickHouse itself slows down for an unrelated reason.
unresolved: sc_positions row density per kit/org under the 15-min lookback window was not measured — needed to judge whether the lifted bbox prefilter stays selective against GPS's ~3s fix rate (Design Risk 2).

Org admin — owns the open Direct order book being matched against

reasons: Multiple genuinely material, ticket-acknowledged design risks remain unresolved and cannot be closed from a read-only prep: IN-vs-equality index pruning (Design Risk 1), GPS density vs bbox selectivity (Design Risk 2), and the W3 concurrency mechanism (no in-repo precedent for either candidate approach).

A currently-red pre-existing test (ScoutRecordCheckInsScheduleTest) sits directly on this ticket's surface and its resolution is entangled with an open sequencing question (whether the schedule can be safely re-enabled before W1/chlocal ships) that this prep cannot settle alone.

AC7's fix touches a shared base class's failure-swallowing contract in spirit even if not in code, and this exact problem has already produced two failed/reverted attempts earlier in this same ticket's history (a watermark guard proven dead code, plus a broader planner/cap design descoped twice) — high risk of the same failure mode recurring under a different name.
Cross-repo dependency: two of the nine ACs (AC5, AC8) are structurally owned outside this repo (chlocal projection, production host verification), which is one of the explicit escalate triggers.

Per the task's own guardrails, this class of design ambiguity (both design risks, the W3 mechanism, per-org-vs-per-kit batching, and the schedule-timing question) was flagged as 'genuinely open... treat as needs-human' rather than something a single prep pass should resolve unilaterally.
